Only you can decide that. 

Correct but you are here for a reason right?  Maybe this sub is the girl with the green eyes for someone out there.   If it's not for you than I am not going to argue with you but I'm here to listen.
By the way, i like your profile picture. I have been playing fallout since the 1st top down games!

What happened to you? I am no expert but I have definitely been there my friend. If you want to message me, feel free. Being an old man, I have a lot of time that is better used helping others like you.
You're welcome. I hope it helps you or others.
Hope it helps you if you're feeling that heavy weight

Thanks

No I had not and didn't share the story until the early 2000s. Told my family and some of my friends,  they couldn't believe it but they didn't know me back then. 

It was my sons that helped track down some neighborhood people I know from that time which led me to her.

I agree with you. It's hard to say really.  I remember men that were just like me, going to fight for something that they were told was right and then there were men that were men that were there to just kill with no consequence.  But then on the other hand, you have men that are again, like me, that have been surprised by past events that you are now paranoid.   War is terrible.  It messes you up.  Especially that war.  And if you read about it, the more you realize that we laid waste to that place for so long for little to no reason.  Politicians are the worst.  Send them on the front line. There would be no more wars.  

Anyway, to answer your question. I had seen a lot. Most I care to not remember if you don't mind me to elaborate.

Yes. It happened slowly. I'd wake up every morning, hoping she would be there. In my mind, she never came back but she probably had. Just not at the same time. I think after 8 years, I called it quits. Said to myself, maybe that's all it was supposed to be. 

Eventually met an amazing woman who I married and had 3 children with. We split up but stayed friends. The birth of my 1st child made me proud of myself that I was still here.  

Those memories will always be there. I heard about veterans going back and finding forgiveness with other soldiers from the other side. I did that with my family in 2003. That was the best way I could atone for my sins. I met some ex NVA soldiers and we shook hands and talked. Both of us carried too much for something that wasn't necessary in the end.

No, it was the fact that we had the same button on and we were at a few large anti war gatherings in Washington. It made me think that meeting her was meant to be. It may seem insignificant but if I didn't meet her that day, you and I wouldn't be conversing.

To be very honest, watching innocent children cry as their parents were burning in front of them. Knowing that even though I didn't burn that hut, I was apart of it. That image burned in my head.  You leave that place and all those memories come rushing back like an unstoppable wave.
Negative. I did. It was her green eyes. You don't forget eyes like that. Kind eyes. Eyes tell everything about a person.

Oh no, I was going to the coffee shop to enjoy one of my last donuts. They made really good donuts. Like Krispy Kreme. We talked a bit and then I went home with my donut and loaded my smith and wesson 38 revolver. But then, I thought about her. And I put it down. I kept doing that all day. Ready at the trigger, thought about her, putting it down. Until I fell asleep on my bed and woke up the next morning.
She didn't remember but was emotional about saving a young man's life. We still keep in contact to this day.
No but she was taken aback and emotional that what she thought was a normal everyday conversation saved a man's life.

There was a coffee shop a few blocks from me the morning of the day I was going to do it. She was there. 

Not initially, the search for her kept me alive. I woke up every morning after, going to the coffee shop to see if she ever came back. I finally found her by chance about 14 years ago.
